**Finding: Compliant (preferred position).**

No most-favoured-nation obligation burdens AbbVie anywhere in the Development and Option Agreement:

- Repeated targeted searches for MFN language ("most favoured/favored nation", "no less favorable", "more favorable", "at least as favorable", "no less advantageous", "comparable terms", "best terms", right-to-match/first-negotiation, price parity) returned no hits.
- I read the full economics in Article 6 (upfront payment, development/regulatory and sales milestones, royalties, the Section 6.5.3 reduction stack, payment, tax, audit provisions) — including the areas carrying redacted `[***]` figures — and none conditions AbbVie's payment terms on terms offered to any Third Party.
- Section 6.5.3(b) (Third Party licence royalty offset) runs in our favour and is not a parity undertaking.
- Section 6.15 affirmatively confirms the Agreement "fully define[s] all consideration, compensation and benefits" between the Parties, foreclosing any implied parity obligation.

No redline proposed; flagging Vendor-favourable pricing mechanics is unnecessary and MFN in our favour would in any event be welcome rather than actionable.
